Name: Ab Wheel (Eccentric)
How to: Roll out from the knees through a longer range than you can return from, taking three to five seconds on the way out. Lower to the floor at the end and reset for the next rep.
Form check: Three to five seconds out · Go past your normal range · Reset from the floor each rep

Name: Ab Wheel (Kneeling)
How to: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders and grip the handles. Tuck the pelvis, then roll out as far as you can keep a flat back and pull yourself back with the abs.
Form check: Tuck the pelvis before rolling · Flat back, no arching · Pull back with the abs not the arms

Name: Ab Wheel (Standing)
How to: Start standing with the wheel on the floor in front of your feet. Roll out to full extension without letting the knees touch, then pull yourself all the way back to standing.
Form check: Knees never touch the floor · Flat back the whole way · Use a wall as a stop while learning

Name: Air Bike
How to: Lie on your back with hands lightly beside your head and lift your shoulders off the floor. Bring one knee toward your chest as you rotate the opposite elbow to meet it. Switch sides in a pedaling motion, extending the free leg out straight.
Form check: Twist elbow to opposite knee · Don't yank the neck · Fully straighten the free leg

Name: Arch Hang
How to: Hang from the bar and pull the shoulder blades down, then arch the chest toward the bar while looking up. Hold briefly and return to a hollow hang.
Form check: Chest up toward the bar · Shoulders stay pulled down · Alternate hollow and arch

Name: Arnold Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Start with the dumbbells in front of the shoulders, palms facing you. Press overhead while rotating the palms to face forward, then reverse the rotation on the way down.
Form check: Rotate smoothly through the press · keep the core braced · don't flare or bounce at the bottom · control the full range

Name: Assisted Pistol Squats
How to: Hold a doorframe or strap for light assistance and lower on one leg with the other held out in front. Use the hands only as much as needed to reach the bottom.
Form check: Free leg stays off the floor · Least assistance that works · Heel stays down

Name: Band Pullaparts
How to: Hold a band with both hands, arms extended straight out in front at shoulder height. Keeping your elbows locked, pull the band apart by driving your hands out to your sides until it meets your chest. Return slowly to the front.
Form check: Keep elbows locked, pull to your chest · Stay tall, don't shrug up

Name: Bar Pullover
How to: Pull hard until the bar reaches the waist, then lean the shoulders forward and rotate over the bar into a straight arm support.
Form check: Pull to the waist before rotating · Lean the shoulders over early · Keep the bar close to the body

Name: Battle Ropes
How to: Anchor a heavy rope at its center and hold one end in each hand with arms at your sides. Drop into a slight athletic quarter-squat and brace your core. Rapidly raise and lower each arm to drive alternating waves down the rope, keeping them fast and continuous.
Form check: Sit into a quarter-squat · Drive fast, tall waves · Keep both arms moving evenly

Name: Behind the Back Bicep Wrist Curl (Barbell)
Bench Dip
How to: Sit on a bench with the hands beside the hips and the feet on the floor in front of you. Slide off the edge and lower until the elbows bend to a right angle, then press back up.
Form check: Elbows point back, not out · Keep the hips close to the bench · Stop at ninety degrees

Name: Bench Press (Barbell)
How to: Lie on a flat bench and take a grip that puts the forearms vertical at the bottom. Unrack and hold the bar over the chest with locked arms. Lower under control until it touches mid-chest, pause, then press back up and squeeze the chest at the top.
Form check: Forearms roughly vertical at the bottom · lower about twice as slowly as you press · drive from the chest · keep the wrists stacked over the elbows

Name: Bench Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set the seat so the handles line up with the mid-chest. Press the handles forward until the arms are extended, then return under control to a stretch.
Form check: Adjust the seat so handles meet the mid-chest · keep the back against the pad · don't let the shoulders roll forward · control the return, don't let it slam

Name: Bench Press - Close Grip (Barbell)
How to: Lie back on a flat bench and grip the bar at about shoulder width. Unrack it and hold it over your chest with arms locked. Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest with elbows tucked close to your sides, then press it back up until your arms lock out.
Form check: Grip about shoulder width · Tuck elbows to your sides · Push through your triceps

Name: Bench Press - Wide Grip (Barbell)
How to: Lie on a flat bench with feet planted. Take a wide, overhand grip a few inches outside shoulder width and unrack the bar over your chest. Lower it to mid-chest with elbows flared out, then press back up to full lockout.
Form check: Grip a hand-width outside shoulders · Pin your shoulder blades back · Flare your elbows out · Lower to mid-chest

Name: Bent Over Row (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the waist, knees slightly bent, back flat until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length. Row them up to your sides, squeezing your back, then lower under control.
Form check: Hinge to near parallel, back flat · Row the bells up to your sides

Name: Bicep Curl (Barbell)
How to: Stand tall holding the bar with an underhand shoulder-width grip and elbows pinned to the sides. Curl to the shoulders by contracting the biceps, then lower under control.
Form check: Elbows stay pinned at the sides · no swinging or hip drive · squeeze at the top · lower slowly to a full stretch

Name: Bicep Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing your thighs. Curl one dumbbell up while rotating your palm to face up, keeping the upper arm still. Lower it and repeat with the other arm.
Form check: Rotate palm up as you lift · Keep upper arms fixed · Alternate arms each rep

Name: Bicycle Crunch
How to: Lie on your back with hands lightly beside your head and lift your shoulders off the floor. Bring one knee toward your chest as you rotate the opposite elbow to meet it. Switch sides in a pedaling motion, extending the free leg out straight.
Form check: Twist elbow to opposite knee · Don't yank the neck · Fully straighten the free leg

Name: Box Squat (Barbell)
How to: Set a flat bench or box behind you and unrack a barbell across your upper back. Stand just in front of the bench with feet shoulder-width. Push your hips back and squat down until you lightly touch the bench, then drive through your heels to stand.
Form check: Push the hips back to the bench · Touch light, don't crash down · Drive up off the bench

Name: Bulgarian Split Squat
How to: Stand a stride in front of a bench and rest the top of the rear foot on it. Lower until the front thigh is parallel to the floor, then drive back up through the front heel.
Form check: Front shin near vertical · Rear foot on the bench · Drive through the front heel

Name: Cable Crunch
How to: Kneel below a high pulley holding the rope by the head. Crunch down by flexing the spine and contracting the abs, bringing the elbows toward the thighs, then return under control.
Form check: Round the spine, flex, don't just hip-fold · keep the hips fixed · drive with the abs, not the arms · don't go so heavy the lower back takes over

Name: Calf Press (Machine)
How to: Sit in the leg press and place just the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform, heels off. Release the safety bars and straighten your legs. Press the platform away by extending your ankles and squeezing the calves, then let your toes come back.
Form check: Balls of feet on the platform edge · Full stretch down, press onto the toes

Name: Chest Dip
How to: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms and a tall chest. Lower until the shoulders drop to elbow height, then press back up to a locked out top position.
Form check: Lower until shoulders reach elbow height · Elbows close to the body · Lock out at the top

Name: Chest Dip (Eccentric)
How to: Jump or step to the top of the parallel bars with straight arms. Lower yourself as slowly as you can until the shoulders reach elbow height, then step off and reset.
Form check: Three to five seconds down · Elbows stay close to the body · Step off and reset each rep

Name: Chest Dip (Weighted)
How to: Attach additional load with a dip belt or vest. Lower through a controlled full range, then press to locked arms without losing shoulder position.
Form check: Record added load only · Full depth · Elbows track back · Full lockout
Equipment: Dip bars; weight belt or vest

Name: Chest Supported Incline Row (Dumbbell)
How to: Set an incline bench and lie chest-down against it with a dumbbell in each hand, neutral grip, arms hanging straight. Squeeze your shoulder blades and row both dumbbells up by driving your elbows back. Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Form check: Keep your chest on the bench · squeeze your shoulder blades first · Drive the elbows back and up

Name: Chin Up (One Arm)
How to: Hang from one hand with a supinated grip and pull until the chin clears the bar. Keep the body from twisting and lower all the way down.
Form check: Chin fully over the bar · Resist the twist · Full straight arm at the bottom

Name: Chin Up (One Arm, Half Range)
How to: Grip the bar with one hand in a supinated grip and pull through the top half of the range only. Lower under control and rest before the next rep.
Form check: Work the top half of the range · Supinated grip · Even work on both arms

Name: Chin Up (One Arm, Towel Assisted)
How to: Hang a towel over the bar next to your working hand. Pull with one arm while the free hand grips the towel low and gives only light help.
Form check: Grip the towel as low as you can · Working arm does the work · Even sets on both sides

Name: Chin Up (Weighted)
Equipment: Pull-up bar; weight belt or vest

Name: Clean
How to: Set up over a barbell with an overhand grip just outside your legs, hips down, back flat and chest up. Drive through the floor and extend your hips explosively, pulling the bar up your body. Shrug and drop under it to catch the bar racked on your shoulders.
Form check: Flat back off the floor · Bar brushes your thighs · Explode through the hips · Drop under to catch

Name: Clean and Jerk
How to: Clean the bar to the shoulders, then dip slightly and drive it overhead with the legs, splitting or squatting under to catch it locked out. Stand to finish.
Form check: Full hip extension on both the clean and the jerk · drive the jerk with the legs, not the arms · punch under a locked-out bar · recover with control, feet in line

Name: Clean and Press
How to: Set up over a barbell with a overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, hips down and back flat. Explosively extend your hips to clean the bar to your shoulders. Brace your core and press the bar overhead until your arms lock out, then lower it back to your shoulders.
Form check: Explode hips to clean · Catch in the front rack · Brace before pressing · Lock out overhead

Name: Clean Pull
How to: Set up over a barbell with an overhand or hook grip just outside your legs, hips down, back flat and chest up. Push through the floor to lift the bar past your knees, then extend your hips, knees and ankles explosively. Shrug tall and let the bar rise without catching it.
Form check: Keep the bar close · Full extend the hips, knees and ankles · No early arm pull

Name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
How to: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing in. Without rotating your wrist, curl one dumbbell up and across your body toward the opposite shoulder. Lower it back to your side and repeat with the other arm.
Form check: Curl across to the opposite shoulder · Neutral grip, no wrist twist

Name: Dead Bug
How to: Lie on your back with arms reaching toward the ceiling and knees bent over your hips at 90 degrees. Press your lower back flat into the floor. Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, then return and switch sides.
Form check: Pin lower back to floor · Lower opposite arm and leg

Name: Deadlift (Barbell)
How to: Set the bar over the mid-foot, hip-width stance, and grip just outside the knees. Take the slack out, flatten the back and brace, then push the floor away and stand tall, dragging the bar up the legs to a locked-out finish.
Form check: Bar over the mid-foot, shins near the bar · flat back, chest up, lats tight · push the floor away rather than yanking · lock the hips and knees together at the top

Name: Deadlift (Trap bar)
How to: Stand in the center of a loaded trap bar and grip both handles. Lower your hips, lift your chest and look forward with a flat back. Push your feet through the floor to stand tall, driving with your legs, then hinge back down under control.
Form check: Stand centered in the bar · Push the floor away with your legs · Drive the knees, not just hips

Name: Decline Bench Press (Barbell)
How to: On a decline bench with feet secured, unrack and hold the bar over the lower chest. Lower under control to the lower chest, then press back up and lock out.
Form check: Bar tracks to the lower chest · keep the shoulder blades squeezed · control down, drive up · keep the wrists stacked over the elbows

Name: Decline Bench Press (Machine)
How to: Set the seat so the handles line up with the mid-chest. Press the handles forward until the arms are extended, then return under control to a stretch.
Form check: Adjust the seat so handles meet the mid-chest · keep the back against the pad · don't let the shoulders roll forward · control the return, don't let it slam

Name: Decline Bench Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set a decline bench in a Smith machine and lie back so the bar sits over your lower chest. Take a overhand grip wider than shoulder width and unlock the bar. Lower it under control to your lower chest, then press it straight up and lock out.
Form check: Grip wider than shoulders · Lower to your lower chest

Name: Decline Crunch
How to: Hook your legs at the top of a decline bench and lie back with your hands beside your head, elbows in. Press your lower back into the bench and curl your shoulders up toward your hips by flexing your abs. Squeeze, then lower under control.
Form check: Curl ribs toward your hips · Hands off the neck, elbows in · No swinging off the bench

Name: Decline Push Up
How to: Place the feet on a box or bench with the hands on the floor. Lower the chest to the floor and press back up while keeping the hips from sagging.
Form check: Higher feet means more load · No sagging hips · Chest to the floor

Name: Diamond Push Up
How to: Place the hands together under the chest so the thumbs and index fingers form a triangle. Lower with the elbows tucked and press back up.
Form check: Hands together under the chest · Elbows stay tucked · Stop if the wrists complain

Name: Drag Curl
How to: Hold a barbell with a palms-up grip and elbows drawn back behind your torso. Curl the bar up while dragging it straight along your body, driving your elbows back so the bar stays close. Lower it down along the same path.
Form check: Drag the bar up your torso · Drive your elbows back · Stop at your lower chest

Name: Dumbbell Row
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the waist, knees slightly bent, back flat until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length. Row them up to your sides, squeezing your back, then lower under control.
Form check: Hinge to near parallel, back flat · Row the bells up to your sides

Name: Elbow to Knee
How to: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite bent knee, hands behind your head. Flex your spine and rotate to bring the opposite elbow toward the crossed knee until your obliques squeeze. Lower under control, then switch legs and sides.
Form check: Bring elbow to the crossed knee · Rotate the torso, not the neck

Name: Elliptical Trainer
How to: Step onto the pedals and take hold of the moving handles. Push down and around through the balls of your feet, driving each pedal through a smooth oval stride. Keep an upright posture and let your legs power the motion.
Form check: Drive the balls of your feet around the oval · Stand tall, don't lean on the handles

Name: EZ Bar Biceps Curl
How to: Stand tall holding an EZ bar at the wide outer handles with palms facing forward and elbows close to your torso. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by flexing the biceps, then lower it slowly back to a full stretch.
Form check: Grip the wide outer handles · Keep elbows close to your torso

Name: Face Pull
How to: Set a rope on a high pulley and grab both ends with palms facing in. Pull the rope toward your face, separating your hands and flaring your elbows out until your hands reach your ears. Keep your upper arms parallel to the floor and lower under control.
Form check: Pull the rope to your forehead · Flare your elbows up and out · Split your hands at the finish

Name: Flutter Kicks
How to: Lie facedown on a bench with your hips at the edge and hold the front for support. Straighten your legs so your toes hang off the floor. Squeeze your glutes to lift both legs, then alternate kicking each leg up and down in small, quick pulses without touching the floor.
Form check: Lift from the glutes, not the low back · Keep both legs straight and pulsing

Name: Front Lever Hold (Tuck)
How to: Hang from a bar and pull the knees to the chest while rotating back so the back faces the floor and the shins point forward. Hold with the arms straight.
Form check: Back parallel to the floor · Knees tight to the chest · Arms stay locked

Name: Front Lever Row
How to: Hold a full front lever with straight legs together and pull the chest to the bar. Lower to straight arms while holding the flat body line.
Form check: Full lever, legs together · Body parallel to the floor · No hip pike

Name: Front Lever Row (Advanced Tuck)
How to: Row while holding an advanced tuck front lever with the knees opened away from the chest and the hips high.
Form check: Open the tuck · Hips stay high · Pull the chest to the bar

Name: Front Lever Row (One Leg)
How to: Row from a front lever with one leg extended and the other tucked. Swap which leg extends between sets.
Form check: One leg long, one tucked · Hips stay level · Even work on both sides

Name: Front Lever Row (Straddle)
How to: Hold a straddle front lever with the legs wide and row the chest toward the bar. Keep the body flat and the arms straight at the bottom.
Form check: Legs wide to lighten the lever · Body flat · Straight arms between reps

Name: Front Lever Row (Tuck)
How to: Hold a tuck front lever and pull the chest toward the bar while keeping the knees tucked and the back flat. Lower to straight arms without losing the shape.
Form check: Hold the tuck through the pull · Back stays parallel to the floor · Straight arms at the bottom

Name: Front Raise (Cable)
How to: Face away from a low pulley gripping the single handle with one hand, arm hanging straight in front of your thigh. Raise the cable forward and up to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend. Lower it back down under control.
Form check: Raise to shoulder height · Don't lean back · Keep the cable taut

Name: Front Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit against an incline bench set to 30 to 60 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms straight down and palms facing back. Raise both arms forward to shoulder height. Lower them back down slowly.
Form check: Keep your back on the pad · Raise straight to the front

Name: Front Squat
How to: Rack the bar across the front of the shoulders with the elbows high, take a shoulder-width stance and brace. Sit straight down between the hips keeping the torso as upright as possible, then drive up through the mid-foot.
Form check: Elbows up, chest tall, don't let them drop · keep the torso vertical · sit between the hips, knees tracking over the toes · brace hard before each rep

Name: Glute Ham Raise
How to: Set your feet against the footplate between the rollers and lie facedown with your knees just behind the pad. Keep your back arched and body straight from knees to head. Lower your torso under control, then drive your toes into the plate and contract the hamstrings to pull back up.
Form check: Straight line, knees to head · Drive the toes into the plate · Control the descent

Name: Goblet Squat
How to: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against the chest. Sit straight down between the hips until the elbows brush the inside of the knees, then stand back up tall.
Form check: Chest up, weight tight to the body · sit between the hips, heels flat · elbows inside the knees at the bottom · brace the core throughout

Name: Hack Squat
How to: Set your shoulders and back against the pad with feet shoulder-width on the platform. Lower under control until the thighs are at least parallel, then press up through the heels without locking the knees hard.
Form check: Keep the whole back flat against the pad · knees track over the toes, don't cave in · control the descent · stop just short of locking the knees

Name: Hammer Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Rest both upper arms on a preacher bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other. Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended, then curl them up until your biceps contract. Keep the neutral grip throughout.
Form check: Keep palms facing each other, no twist · Upper arms flat on the pad

Name: Handstand Push Up
How to: Kick up to a wall handstand with the hands on parallettes or blocks. Lower until the head passes below the hands, then press all the way back to a locked out handstand.
Form check: Full range below the hands · Lock the elbows at the top · Keep the body straight, not arched

Name: Handstand Push-Up (Freestanding)
How to: Hold a freestanding handstand, lower to full depth, and press back to straight arms with no wall support. Correct the balance with the fingers through the whole rep.
Form check: No wall at any point · Full depth then full lockout · Keep the body line tight

Name: Hang Clean
How to: Hold the bar at mid-thigh with a shoulder-width overhand or hook grip, back flat and torso leaning slightly forward. Aggressively extend the hips, knees, and ankles, then pull under the bar and catch it in a front-rack squat.
Form check: Lean the torso slightly over the bar · Triple-extend explosively · Keep the bar brushing the thighs · Snap elbows into the front rack

Name: Hang Snatch
How to: Take a wide overhand or hook grip with the bar at the hips, feet under the hips and turned out, spine extended and chest up. Violently extend the hips, knees, and ankles, then pull under and catch the bar overhead in a squat.
Form check: Take a wide grip at the hips · Keep the bar close on the pull · Extend hips, knees, and ankles · Punch under to lockout in a squat

Name: Hanging Bent-Leg Raise
How to: From a hang, straighten the legs a little and lift the thighs above hip height. Tuck the pelvis at the top, then lower with control and stop any swing before the next rep.
Form check: Thighs above hip height · Tuck the pelvis at the top · Stay quiet on the bar

Name: Hanging Knee Raise
How to: Hang from a bar with straight arms and pull the shoulders down away from the ears. Lift the knees toward the chest and lower them under control without swinging.
Form check: Pull the shoulders down first · No swing · Lower slower than you lift

Name: Hanging Straight-Leg Raise
How to: Hang with straight legs together and lift them until they are at least parallel to the floor. Lower slowly and let the swing settle before starting the next rep.
Form check: Straight legs to horizontal or higher · Lower with control · Reset the swing between reps

Name: Headstand Push-Up (Freestanding)
How to: Kick up to a freestanding handstand and lower under control until the head touches the floor. Press back up while making small balance corrections with the fingers.
Form check: Balance with the fingertips · Lower under control · Bail to the side if you lose it

Name: Headstand Push-Up (Wall)
How to: Set up in a wall handstand and lower until the head touches the floor between the hands. Press back to straight arms while the wall keeps you upright.
Form check: Head and hands make a triangle · Press evenly with both arms · Keep the ribs down

Name: Headstand Push-Up (Wall, Eccentric)
How to: Kick up to a handstand with the heels on the wall. Lower slowly until the head touches the floor between the hands, then come down from the wall and reset instead of pressing back up.
Form check: Three to five seconds down · Head lands between the hands · Come off the wall to reset

Name: Heel Taps
How to: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and shoulder-width apart, and arms extended at your sides. Crunch your torso up and to one side, reaching your hand toward that heel. Return to center, then bend to the other side and touch that heel.
Form check: Crunch to the side · Reach for your heel

Name: Hip Thrust (Barbell)
How to: Sit with the upper back on a bench and the bar across the hips. Drive through the heels to lift the hips to a straight line from knees to shoulders, then lower under control.
Form check: Tuck the chin and keep the ribs down · drive through the heels · squeeze the glutes hard at lockout · don't hyperextend the lower back at the top

Name: Incline Bench Press (Barbell)
How to: Lie back on an incline bench and grip the bar at medium width. Unrack it and hold it straight over your upper chest with arms locked. Lower the bar slowly to your upper chest, then drive it back up until your arms lock out.
Form check: Grip at medium width · Lower to your upper chest · Keep shoulder blades pinned

Name: Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell)
How to: On a 30-45 degree incline, start with the dumbbells at the upper chest, palms forward. Press up and slightly together until the arms are extended, then lower under control to a full stretch.
Form check: Keep the shoulder blades pulled back and down · lower to a controlled stretch, don't bounce · elbows around 45 degrees, not flared to 90 · press in a slight arc toward the top

Name: Incline Bench Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set an incline bench under the Smith machine, with the bar set where your arms are almost fully extended. Lie back and grip slightly wider than shoulder width, then unrack. Lower the bar to your upper chest, then press up and slightly back to lockout.
Form check: Set the bar over upper chest · Grip just outside shoulders · Drive up and slightly back

Name: Incline Push Ups
How to: Put the hands on a bench, box or bar with the body in a straight line. Lower the chest to the surface and press back up, lowering the hand height as you get stronger.
Form check: Lower hands means harder · Straight line from head to heels · Chest touches each rep

Name: Inverted Row
How to: Set up with the body fully parallel to the floor under the bar or rings. Pull the chest to the bar, pause, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Body parallel to the floor · Pause at the top · No sagging hips

Name: Inverted Row (Archer)
How to: From a horizontal row position, pull toward one hand while the other arm straightens out to the side. Alternate sides each rep.
Form check: Pull to one side at a time · Far arm straightens · Hips stay square

Name: Inverted Row (Bent Legs)
How to: Hang under a bar with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor. Pull the chest to the bar keeping the body in one line, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Knees bent to lighten the load · Chest touches the bar · Hips stay up

Name: Inverted Row (Feet Elevated)
How to: Put the feet on a box so the body sits close to horizontal under the bar. Pull the chest to the bar and lower slowly without letting the hips drop.
Form check: Feet elevated to the bar height · Hips stay lifted · Chest to the bar each rep

Name: Inverted Row (Incline)
How to: Set a bar or rings at chest height and hold on with the body almost upright. Walk the feet forward a little and pull the chest to the bar, then lower under control.
Form check: Body near upright · Pull the chest to the bar · Squeeze the shoulder blades

Name: Inverted Row (One Arm)
How to: Set up horizontally under the bar and row with a single arm while the body stays rigid and square. Switch arms between sets.
Form check: One hand only · Resist the twist · Body stays parallel to the floor

Name: Inverted Row (One Arm, Assisted)
How to: Row horizontally with most of the load on one arm while the other hand gives light support on the bar or a strap. Switch sides between sets.
Form check: One arm does most of the work · Support hand stays light · Keep the hips square

Name: Inverted Row (Straight Legs)
How to: Hang under the bar with straight legs and the heels on the floor at roughly forty five degrees. Pull the chest to the bar and lower with control.
Form check: Straight legs, heels down · One line from head to heels · Full arm extension at the bottom

Name: Inverted Row (Weighted)
How to: Add external load with a vest or plates while keeping the body rigid. Pull the chest to the bar or rings, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Record added load only · Body angle stays fixed · Chest reaches the hands · Control the descent
Equipment: Bar or gymnastic rings; weight vest or plates

Name: Inverted Row (Wide Grip)
How to: Row from the horizontal position with the hands set wider than shoulder width. Pull the chest to the bar and squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Form check: Wider grip loads the upper back · Squeeze the shoulder blades · Keep the body flat

Name: Jackknife Sit Up
How to: Lie flat with your arms extended overhead and legs straight. Exhale and raise your legs and torso at the same time, reaching your hands toward your feet so your body forms a V. Lower your arms and legs back down under control.
Form check: Raise legs and torso as one · Keep legs straight, not bent · Meet hands to feet up top

Name: Jumping Lunge
How to: Drop into a lunge with the front knee bent over your foot and the rear knee nearly touching the floor. Extend explosively through both legs to jump as high as you can, swinging the arms up. Land softly back in the lunge and absorb through both legs.
Form check: Drop into a deep lunge · Front knee stacked over the foot · Explode up through both legs · Land back in the lunge

Name: Kettlebell Clean
How to: Place a kettlebell between your feet, push your hips back, and grip it one-handed with eyes forward. Extend through the legs and hips to pull the bell up, rotating your hand around it to catch cleanly at the shoulder. Lower and repeat.
Form check: Keep the bell tight to the body · Wrap the rack, don't bang it

Name: Kettlebell High Pull
How to: Stand in a wide sumo stance with a kettlebell between your feet and grip it with both hands, hips set back and chest up. Drive through your legs and hips to pull the kettlebell explosively up to chest height, leading with high elbows. Lower it back between your legs.
Form check: Drive through legs and hips · Explode the bell to chest height · Lead with high elbows · Keep your chest up, back flat

Name: Kettlebell Snatch
How to: Set a kettlebell between your feet, bend the knees, and sit the hips back with eyes forward. Swing the bell back between your legs, then reverse hard and drive through the hips to punch it straight to lockout overhead in one motion.
Form check: Drive the swing with the hips · Keep the bell close on the way up · Spear the hand through at lockout

Name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up
How to: Lie on your back and press one kettlebell to a locked-out arm above your shoulder. Keeping the elbow locked and eyes on the bell, rise to your feet through a series of controlled steps. Stand fully, then reverse each step back to the floor.
Form check: Press the bell to a locked arm · Keep the elbow locked throughout · Keep your eyes on the bell · Rise and reverse one step at a time

Name: Knee Raise Parallel Bars
How to: Support yourself on the raise station with your forearms on the pads and back against the rest, legs hanging straight down. Raise your knees up toward your chest by curling your hips and contracting your abs. Lower them slowly to the hang.
Form check: Curl your hips under, not just knees · Keep your legs from swinging

Name: L-Sit Hold
How to: Support on parallettes or bars with straight arms, then lift straight legs until they are parallel to the floor. Point the toes and hold with the shoulders pushed away from the ears.
Form check: Legs straight and parallel to the floor · Toes pointed · Shoulders pushed down

Name: L-Sit Hold (Advanced Tuck)
How to: From the tuck position, open the knees to roughly a right angle so the thighs move away from the chest. Hold with a flat back and the hips level with the shoulders.
Form check: Open the tuck to ninety degrees · Keep the back flat · Hips level with the shoulders

Name: L-Sit Hold (Foot-Supported)
How to: Sit with straight legs and press your hands into the floor or parallettes beside the hips. Push the shoulders down and lift the body so the heels rest lightly on the ground and carry almost no weight.
Form check: Push the floor away · Heels light, not loaded · Straight arms throughout

Name: L-Sit Hold (Straddle)
How to: Hold an L-sit and open the legs into a wide straddle. Keep both legs at hip height or higher and press the shoulders down for the whole hold.
Form check: Open the legs wide · Keep them level or higher · Straight knees

Name: L-Sit Hold (Tuck)
How to: Support yourself on parallettes or bars with straight arms and pull both knees tightly to the chest. Hold with the shoulders pressed down and the hips lifted clear of the floor.
Form check: Knees tight to the chest · Shoulders pressed down · Lift the hips, do not hang

Name: Lateral Box Jump
How to: Stand tall beside a short box with feet hip-width. Dip quickly into a quarter squat to load, then explode up and sideways to land on top of the box. Absorb softly in a partial squat with both feet, then step down and reset on the other side.
Form check: Quick dip, jump sideways · Land balanced on the box · Step down, don't jump down

Name: Lateral Raise (Cable)
How to: Place a flat bench between two opposing low pulleys and sit on it. Grab each handle with the opposite hand so the cables cross under your knees. Raise both handles out to your sides to shoulder height, then lower slowly against the tension.
Form check: Cross the cables under your knees · Raise out to shoulder height

Name: Lunge (Barbell)
How to: With the bar on the upper back, step forward and lower until the back knee is just off the floor and the front thigh is parallel. Drive through the front heel back to standing.
Form check: Torso upright, core braced · front knee stays over the foot, not past the toes · drive through the front heel · control the descent, don't drop

Name: Lying Bent-Leg Raise
How to: Lie on your back and extend the shins so the legs are only slightly bent. Raise them until the hips are fully flexed, then lower under control with the lower back pinned down.
Form check: Longer lever, same flat back · Control the lowering · Shorten the range if the back lifts

Name: Lying Knee Raise
How to: Lie on your back with the hands beside the hips and press the lower back into the floor. Draw the knees toward the chest, then lower them slowly without letting the back arch.
Form check: Low back stays flat · Slow on the way down · Stop before the back lifts

Name: Lying Straight-Leg Raise
How to: Lie flat with straight legs held together. Lift them until they point at the ceiling, then lower slowly until the heels hover just above the floor with the back still flat.
Form check: Straight knees · Heels stop just off the floor · Keep the back flat all set

Name: Muscle Up
How to: Pull explosively until the bar or rings reach the lower chest. Roll the shoulders forward over the top and press out to a locked support with no leg swing.
Form check: Pull to the lower chest, not the chin · Lean over the bar at the transition · No kip

Name: Muscle Up (Eccentric)
How to: Start at the top in a straight arm support and lower slowly through the transition until you finish in a hang. Take the transition as slowly as you can control it.
Form check: Slowest through the transition · Keep the rings or bar close · Finish in a full hang

Name: Muscle Up (Kipping)
How to: From a hang, swing the legs forward and drive the hips up while pulling the bar toward the waist. Roll the shoulders over the top and press out to a straight arm support.
Form check: Time the hip drive with the pull · Roll the shoulders forward early · Finish with straight arms

Name: Negative Pull Up
How to: Jump or step so your chin starts above the bar. Lower yourself for three to five seconds until the arms are straight, then step down and reset for the next rep.
Form check: Three to five seconds down · Finish with straight arms · Step down and reset each rep

Name: Nordic Hamstrings Curls
How to: Anchor the heels under a bar or have a partner hold them. Keep the hips straight and lower the body toward the floor as slowly as you can, catching with the hands.
Form check: Hips stay open, not folded · Lower as slowly as possible · Catch with the hands

Name: One Arm Push Up
How to: Set the feet wide and put one hand under the chest with the other behind the back. Lower the chest to the floor and press up while keeping the hips square.
Form check: Feet wide for balance · Hips stay square to the floor · Chest touches the floor

Name: One-Arm One-Leg Plank
How to: From a forearm plank, lift one arm and the opposite leg a few inches off the floor. Hold without letting the hips rotate, then set them down and switch sides.
Form check: Lift opposite arm and leg · Keep the hips square to the floor · Short strict holds

Name: Overhead Curl (Cable)
How to: Set both pulleys high and grab a handle in each hand. Stand tall between them with arms extended out at shoulder height, palms up. Curl both hands toward your ears until your biceps peak, then straighten your arms back out.
Form check: Keep elbows high at shoulder level · Curl your knuckles toward your ears · Move only the forearms

Name: Overhead Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set a bench with back support under the Smith bar and sit so the bar sits just above your shoulders. Unrack it with a overhand grip and press the bar straight up until your arms extend. Lower under control to the top of your chest.
Form check: Follow the fixed bar path up · Lower the bar to upper chest

Name: Overhead Squat
How to: Take a wide snatch grip and press the barbell to full lockout overhead, feet slightly wider than the shoulders. Push the bar back so it sits over your midfoot. Squat down as deep as mobility allows while keeping the bar overhead, then drive up.
Form check: Wide snatch grip, elbows locked · Keep the bar over midfoot · Actively push the bar up · Squat deep, bar stays back

Name: Pike Push-Up (Feet Elevated)
How to: Put the feet on a box so the hips stack higher over the shoulders. Lower the head toward the floor between the hands and press back up with the elbows tracking forward.
Form check: Higher box means more vertical load · Stack the hips over the shoulders · Head between the hands

Name: Pike Pushup
How to: Start in a pushup position and walk the feet in so the hips lift high and the body makes an upside down V. Bend the elbows to lower the crown of the head toward the floor, then press back up.
Form check: Hips high, body in a V · Head lowers between the hands · Elbows track forward

Name: Pistol Squat
How to: Stand on one leg with the other held straight out in front. Lower all the way to the bottom and stand back up with no support and no bouncing.
Form check: Full depth on one leg · Free leg never touches · Heel stays flat

Name: Pistol Squat (Box)
How to: Stand on one leg in front of a box, hold the free leg forward, and lower until the hips lightly touch the box before standing on the same leg. Reduce box height as strength improves.
Form check: Touch rather than sit · Knee tracks over toes · Free foot stays clear · No rocking for momentum

Name: Pistol Squat (Counterweighted)
How to: Hold a light plate or dumbbell out in front of the chest to balance the load. Lower on one leg to the bottom and stand back up.
Form check: Counterweight helps balance · Free leg straight in front · Drop the weight as balance improves

Name: Planche
How to: Hold the body horizontal with the legs together and the arms locked straight. The whole body stays in one line parallel to the floor.
Form check: Legs together and straight · Body parallel to the floor · Push down hard through the whole hold

Name: Planche (Advanced Tuck)
How to: From the tuck planche, open the knees so the thighs move away from the chest and flatten the back. Hold with the hips level and the arms locked straight.
Form check: Open the tuck, flatten the back · Hips level with the shoulders · Keep pushing the floor away

Name: Planche (Straddle)
How to: Hold a straight-arm planche with the legs separated to shorten the lever. Keep the body horizontal and gradually narrow the straddle as strength improves.
Form check: Arms locked · Hips level with shoulders · No piking · Point the toes

Name: Planche (Tuck)
How to: Support on the floor or parallettes with straight arms, lean forward, and pull both knees to the chest with the hips lifted to shoulder height. Hold with a rounded upper back.
Form check: Hips up to shoulder height · Knees tight to the chest · Round the upper back and push down

Name: Planche Lean
How to: Start in a straight-arm push-up position with the hands slightly turned out. Lean the shoulders forward past the wrists while keeping the body rigid and the shoulder blades protracted.
Form check: Arms locked · Shoulders ahead of wrists · Push the floor away · No hip sag

Name: Planche Lean (Tuck)
How to: Hold a deep planche lean and lift one knee at a time toward the chest so both feet leave the floor briefly. Keep the shoulders forward and the arms locked.
Form check: Lean first, then tuck · Both feet leave the floor · Arms stay straight

Name: Planche Push-Up
How to: Hold a full planche with the legs together and the body horizontal. Lower the chest toward the floor and press back to straight arms with the feet never touching down.
Form check: Legs together and straight · Body parallel to the floor · Feet never touch

Name: Planche Push-Up (Advanced Tuck)
How to: Hold an advanced tuck planche with the back flat and the knees away from the chest. Lower under control and press back up while keeping the hips level.
Form check: Flat back throughout · Hips level with the shoulders · Stop the set when the tuck closes

Name: Planche Push-Up (Straddle)
How to: Hold a straddle planche with the legs wide and the body horizontal. Bend the arms to lower, then press back to straight arms without dropping the hips.
Form check: Legs wide to shorten the lever · Body stays parallel to the floor · Full lockout at the top

Name: Planche Push-Up (Tuck)
How to: Hold a tuck planche with the knees at the chest and the hips high. Bend the arms to lower the chest, then press back up without letting the feet touch down.
Form check: Feet never touch the floor · Hips stay high · Short sets

Name: Plank
How to: Rest on the forearms and toes with the elbows under the shoulders. Brace the abdominals and glutes to hold a straight line from head to heels for the prescribed time.
Form check: Elbows under shoulders · Ribs down · No sagging or piking · Breathe steadily

Name: Plate Front Raise
How to: Stand tall gripping a weight plate at the 3 and 9 o'clock edges, palms facing each other, arms extended down with a slight elbow bend. Raise the plate forward to shoulder height. Lower it back down under control.
Form check: Grip at 3 and 9 · Don't rock the torso

Name: Power Clean
How to: From a deadlift setup, pull the bar explosively past the knees, extend the hips, ankles and knees, then whip the elbows through to catch the bar on the front of the shoulders in a partial squat.
Form check: Keep the bar close to the body · explode through the hips, knees and ankles · fast elbows to rack the bar · catch soft in a quarter squat

Name: Power Snatch
How to: Stand over the bar with a wide grip, feet under your hips, hips down and chest up. Pull the bar from the floor and accelerate it past your hips with a powerful snap of the hips and knees. Pull yourself under and catch it locked out overhead in a partial squat, then stand.
Form check: Wide grip, bar brushing close · Accelerate past the hips · Full snap of hips and knees · Punch under to lockout

Name: Preacher Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Rest both upper arms on a preacher bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other. Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended, then curl them up until your biceps contract. Keep the neutral grip throughout.
Form check: Keep palms facing each other, no twist · Upper arms flat on the pad

Name: Pull Up
How to: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width. Pull until the chin clears the bar, then lower all the way to straight arms under control.
Form check: Chin fully over the bar · Lower to straight arms · Keep the body from swinging

Name: Pull Up (Archer)
How to: Pull up with a wide grip and travel toward one hand while the opposite arm stays straight along the bar. Alternate sides each rep.
Form check: One arm straight like drawing a bow · Pull high before you shift · Alternate sides

Name: Pull Up (Band)
How to: Loop a band under the knee or foot, or rest one foot on a low box. Pull to full range with the chin over the bar and use only as much help as you need.
Form check: Use the least help that works · Full range every rep · Drop the assistance as you get stronger

Name: Pull Up (Belly Button)
How to: Pull as high as you can while leaning back hard so the bar travels toward the navel. Keep the pull smooth rather than kipping into position.
Form check: Bar aims for the navel · Big lean back · No kip

Name: Pull Up (Chest to Bar)
How to: Pull explosively while leaning back so the bar meets the lower chest. Keep the elbows driving down and behind you at the top.
Form check: Bar touches the lower chest · Lean back at the top · Drive the elbows down

Name: Pull Up (Close Grip)
How to: Take an overhand grip narrower than shoulder width. Pull to the bar keeping the elbows close to the body, then lower to a full hang.
Form check: Hands inside shoulder width · Elbows brush the ribs · Full hang at the bottom

Name: Pull Up (False Grip)
How to: Hook the wrists over the rings or bar so the heel of the hand sits on top of the grip. Pull until the rings reach the lower chest while holding that wrist position throughout.
Form check: Heel of the hand on top of the ring · Pull to the lower chest · Expect sore wrists at first

Name: Pull Up (L-Sit)
How to: Hold both legs straight out in front at hip height, then perform full pull ups without letting the legs drop.
Form check: Legs stay parallel to the floor · No swinging · Drop the set when the legs sag

Name: Pull Up (One Arm, Eccentric)
How to: Start at the top with one arm and the chin over the bar. Lower as slowly as you can through the full range until the arm is straight.
Form check: Start at the top · Fight the whole way down · Stop when the descent turns into a drop

Name: Pull Up (Typewriter)
How to: Pull to the top with a wide grip, then shift sideways over one hand while the other arm straightens. Move back across the bar and lower under control.
Form check: Stay high while you travel · Straighten the trailing arm · Even reps on both sides

Name: Pull Up (Weighted)
How to: Attach additional load with a belt or vest. Start from a full hang, pull until the chin clears the bar, and lower under control.
Form check: Record added load only · Full hang · Chin over bar · No kipping
Equipment: Pull-up bar; weight belt or vest

Name: Push Press
How to: Hold the bar on the front of the shoulders with a shoulder-width grip and elbows up. Dip briefly at the knees, then drive explosively through the legs to launch the bar overhead and lock the arms out. Lower under control to the shoulders and reset.
Form check: Short, vertical dip, do not lean forward · drive with the legs, not just the arms · finish with the bar stacked over the mid-foot · brace the core throughout

Name: Push Up
How to: Set the hands slightly wider than the shoulders with the body in a straight line. Lower until the chest is just off the floor, then press back to locked arms.
Form check: Elbows at about forty five degrees · Hips in line with the shoulders · Full lockout at the top

Name: Push Up - Close Grip
How to: Perform pushups keeping the elbows tucked close to the ribs the whole way down. The hands sit under the lower chest rather than out wide.
Form check: Elbows brush the ribs · Hands under the lower chest · Expect more triceps work

Name: Push-Up (Archer)
How to: Take a wide hand position and lower toward one hand while the other arm straightens out to the side. Press back up and alternate sides.
Form check: Straighten the far arm · Chest lands over the working hand · Alternate each rep

Name: Push-Up (One Arm, Incline)
How to: Place one hand on a bench or box with the other behind the back and the feet wide. Lower the chest to the surface and press back up, then switch sides.
Form check: Feet wide for balance · Lower the surface as you progress · Hips stay square

Name: Push-Up (Pseudo Planche)
How to: Place the hands lower beside the torso, lean the shoulders forward past the hands, and perform push-ups without losing the forward lean.
Form check: Shoulders remain ahead of hands · Body stays rigid · Elbows track close · Use a pain-free wrist angle

Name: Push-Up (Rings Turned Out)
How to: Set the rings just off the floor and turn them out so the palms face forward at the top. Lower to the chest and press back up, restoring the turnout each rep.
Form check: Turn the rings out at lockout · Elbows stay close · Control the wobble

Name: Push-Up (Rings Turned Out, Archer)
How to: Perform archer pushups on rings turned out at the top. Lower toward one ring while the other arm straightens, then press back and turn the rings out again.
Form check: Turnout at the top of each rep · Far arm straightens · Alternate sides

Name: Push-Up (Rings Turned Out, Pseudo Planche)
How to: On rings turned out, lean the shoulders forward and perform push-ups while keeping the rings stable and the forward lean consistent.
Form check: Rings remain turned out · Shoulders ahead of hands · No ring drift · Control the bottom

Name: Push-Up (Rings)
How to: Set the rings just off the floor and hold them at shoulder width. Lower the chest to ring height and press back up while keeping the rings from wobbling.
Form check: Rings stay under the shoulders · Full range each rep · Squeeze the rings hard

Name: Push-Up (Rings, Wide)
How to: Set the rings a few inches off the floor and take a wide hand position. Lower the chest between the rings and press back up while stopping them from drifting.
Form check: Wide hands, deeper stretch · Rings stay steady · Body in one line

Name: Push-Up (Uneven)
How to: Put one hand on a low block or ball and the other on the floor. Perform pushups so the lower arm takes most of the load, then switch sides.
Form check: Lower hand does most of the work · Keep the hips square · Even sets on both sides

Name: Push-Up (Wall)
How to: Stand an arm length from a wall and place the hands on it at chest height. Bend the elbows to bring the chest to the wall, then press back to straight arms.
Form check: Body stays in one line · Elbows at about forty five degrees · Step the feet back to make it harder

Name: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Cable)
How to: Set both pulleys above head height and grab the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left so the cables cross in front. Pull your arms apart and back in a wide arc until they reach out to your sides. Squeeze the rear delts, then return under control.
Form check: Cross the cables in front · Sweep wide and back to your sides · Keep arms level with your shoulders

Name: Reverse Curl (Cable)
How to: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and grip it at shoulder width with palms facing down. Stand tall with elbows tucked to your sides. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders until your biceps contract, then lower it slowly until your arms are straight.
Form check: Keep palms facing down · Pin elbows to your sides · Curl up without leaning back

Name: Reverse Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing down, arms fully extended. Keep your elbows close to your sides and curl the weights up until your biceps contract. Lower them slowly until your arms are straight, holding the palms-down grip.
Form check: Keep palms facing down · Elbows stay close to your sides

Name: Reverse Lunge (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Step backward with one leg and lower your hips until both knees bend near 90 degrees and the back knee nearly touches the floor. Drive through the front heel back to standing, then alternate legs.
Form check: Step straight back · Keep weight on front heel

Name: Ring Dip (Rings Turned Out)
How to: Perform ring dips and finish each press by turning the rings out so the palms face forward at the top. Hold that turnout for a moment before the next rep.
Form check: Turn the rings out at the top · Elbows stay in · Start with a short turned out hold

Name: Ring Dips
How to: Support on rings with straight arms and the rings held close to the hips. Lower under control to the bottom, then press back up while stopping the rings from drifting out.
Form check: Keep the rings pinned near the hips · Slow and controlled · Straight arms at the top

Name: Rope Straight Arm Pulldown
How to: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand a couple feet back with a staggered stance. Hinge forward from the hips with a straight back and take the rope with arms extended overhead. Sweep your arms down to your thighs, then control back up.
Form check: Spread the rope at your thighs · Arms straight, drive from the lats

Name: Russian Twist (Bodyweight)
How to: Sit with the knees bent and torso leaned back, feet up or down. Rotate the torso to touch the weight or hands to each side under control.
Form check: Rotate through the trunk, not just the arms · keep the chest up and back braced · move under control, no flinging · keep the core tight throughout

Name: Scapular Pull Ups
How to: Hang from the bar with straight arms. Without bending the elbows, pull the shoulder blades down and together so the body rises an inch or two, then lower back to a relaxed hang.
Form check: Elbows stay straight · Move only the shoulder blades · Pause at the top of each rep

Name: Seated Cable Row - Bar Wide Grip
Seated Calf Raise
How to: Sit with the pad on the lower thighs and the balls of the feet on the block. Lower the heels to a stretch, then press up as high as possible onto the toes.
Form check: Full stretch at the bottom · press up as high as possible · pause at the top · keep the reps smooth and controlled

Name: Seated Incline Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length with elbows close to your sides. Curl the weights up while rotating your palms to face up, until your biceps contract. Lower slowly and rotate back to the start.
Form check: Keep elbows pinned to your sides · Rotate palms up as you curl · Untwist to neutral on the way down

Name: Seated Leg Curl (Machine)
How to: Sit with the pad on the lower calves and thighs secured. Curl the heels down and back under the seat, squeeze, then return under control.
Form check: Keep the thighs pinned under the pad · full range curl · squeeze the hamstrings · control the return

Name: Seated Overhead Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit on a bench with back support and bring a dumbbell to each shoulder, palms facing forward. Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms extend and the weights nearly meet. Lower them under control back to shoulder height.
Form check: Press until dumbbells nearly meet · Keep your back on the pad

Name: Seated Palms Up Wrist Curl
How to: Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up. Rest your forearms along your thighs so the wrists hang just past your knees. Let the dumbbells roll down toward your fingers, then curl them up by flexing your wrists fully.
Form check: Roll the bells down to your fingers · Curl up, only the wrists move

Name: Seated Triceps Press
How to: Sit on a bench with back support and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, arms locked out. Keep your elbows pointing forward and lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows. Press it back up to full extension.
Form check: Point your elbows forward, not out · Lower behind your head

Name: Shoulder Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Seated or standing, start with the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward. Press overhead until the arms extend, then lower under control to the shoulders.
Form check: Brace the core, don't arch the lower back · press slightly in, not straight out · full lockout overhead · control the weight back to the shoulders

Name: Shrimp Squat (Advanced)
How to: Hold the rear foot behind you and lower until the back knee touches, keeping the torso upright and the balance steady with no assistance.
Form check: Upright torso · Smooth touch and stand · No wobble at the bottom

Name: Shrimp Squat (Beginner)
How to: Hold one foot behind you with the same side hand and lower on the other leg until the back knee touches a pad. Use a light support with the free hand.
Form check: Back knee touches a pad · Free hand for balance · Torso stays upright

Name: Shrimp Squat (Intermediate)
How to: Hold the rear foot with the same side hand and lower to the back knee without any hand support. Stand back up on the working leg.
Form check: No hand support · Back knee taps the floor · Keep the chest tall

Name: Shrug (Barbell)
How to: Hold the bar in front of the thighs with straight arms. Shrug the shoulders straight up toward the ears, hold briefly, then lower under control.
Form check: Lift straight up, don't roll the shoulders · keep the arms straight · squeeze the traps at the top · control the lowering

Name: Single Arm Cable Crossover
How to: Set the pulley high and take the handle in one hand, stepping forward so the arm is extended out and back. Keep your chest up and pull the handle down and across your body toward the opposite hip. Squeeze the chest, then return slowly to the stretch.
Form check: Pull down across to the far hip · Stand tall, don't twist the torso

Name: Single Arm Curl (Cable)
How to: Grab a single handle at the low pulley and step back so the cable stays taut. Pin your upper arm to your side and keep it still. Curl the handle up toward your shoulder by squeezing the biceps, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
Form check: Pin your upper arm to your side · Keep the cable taut at the bottom

Name: Single Arm Lat Pulldown
How to: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and sit with the knee pad snug against your thighs. Grip the handle with your palm facing forward and arm extended overhead. Pull it down, driving your elbow to your side, then control it back up.
Form check: Drive your elbow down to your ribs · Reach tall for a full stretch · Keep shoulders level, no twist

Name: Single Arm Tricep Extension (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit or stand tall and raise a dumbbell overhead in one hand with the arm fully extended. Keep your upper arm close to your head and pointing up. Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending the elbow, then extend your arm to press it back overhead.
Form check: Keep the upper arm pointing up · Lower behind your head

Name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
How to: Lie on your back with feet flat and knees bent, then lift one knee toward your chest. Drive through the heel of your planted foot and extend your hip to raise your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line. Lower under control to the floor.
Form check: Drive through your planted heel · Keep both hips level as you rise

Name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight)
How to: Stand on one leg with a soft knee and hinge at the hips, letting the free leg travel back as the chest lowers. Return by driving the hips forward.
Form check: Hinge at the hips, not the waist · Back stays flat · Hips stay level

Name: Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Barbell)
How to: Set a loaded barbell across your upper back and place the balls of your feet on a block or plate with heels hanging off. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing the calves hard. Lower your heels below the block for a deep stretch.
Form check: Rise to full tip-toe · Sink the heels below the block

Name: Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a sturdy object for balance and place the balls of both feet on a dumbbell handle, heels on the floor. Rise onto your toes as high as you can by squeezing the calves. Lower your heels back toward the floor under control for a full stretch.
Form check: Rise as high as you can · Steady the wobbling handle

Name: Sissy Squat (Weighted)
How to: Grip a squat rack upright with one hand and hold a weight plate against your chest with the other, feet shoulder-width and up on your toes. Lower by driving your knees forward and leaning your torso back in a straight line. Pull with your quads to rise back up.
Form check: Drive your knees forward · Keep your body in a straight line

Name: Sit Up
How to: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet anchored, and hands behind your head. Curl your torso up off the floor toward your knees, leading with your chest. Lower back down with control until your shoulders touch.
Form check: Don't yank on your neck · Roll up through the spine · Lead with your chest

Name: Sled Push
How to: Load the sled and grip the handles with your arms fully extended. Set an athletic stance with a forward body lean and a flat back. Drive the sled forward by powering through the balls of your feet, fully extending the hips and knees with every stride.
Form check: Arms long, back flat · Push through the balls of the feet · Fully extend hips and knees

Name: Snatch
How to: From a wide grip, pull the bar explosively from the floor, extend the hips and pull under to catch it overhead in a full squat, then stand to lockout.
Form check: Wide grip, bar close and over the mid-foot · explode through the hips · pull under fast to a locked-out catch · stay tight and stand tall to finish

Name: Spider Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest supported and shoulders near the top. Let your arms hang straight down holding a dumbbell in each hand. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders, then lower them under control to a full stretch.
Form check: Lie chest-down on the bench · Let arms hang straight down

Name: Split Jerk
How to: Rack the bar across your front delts, feet under your hips. Dip straight down by bending the knees, then drive up explosively and punch the bar overhead. As it rises, split one foot forward and one back into a lunge and lock the arms, then recover the feet to standing.
Form check: Dip straight down, torso tall · Drive through legs, not arms · Split feet front and back · Catch with arms locked out

Name: Squat (Assisted)
How to: Hold a doorframe, pole or suspension strap and sit back into a squat. Use the hands for balance and only as much pull as you need to reach depth.
Form check: Use the hands for balance · Sit back and down · Heels stay flat

Name: Squat (Assisted, Deep)
How to: Using the same light support, lower all the way until the hamstrings meet the calves. Hold the bottom briefly, then stand back up.
Form check: Go to full depth · Pause at the bottom · Keep the heels down

Name: Squat (Barbell)
How to: Set the bar just below shoulder height, step under it and rest it across your upper back. Drive through your legs to unrack, step back to a shoulder-width stance with toes slightly out. Sit the hips back and bend the knees until the hamstrings meet the calves, then drive up through the mid-foot to standing.
Form check: Head up, back flat throughout · brace before you descend · inhale down, exhale up · push the floor away through heel and mid-foot · knees track over the toes

Name: Squat (Bodyweight)
How to: Stand with the feet about shoulder width and the toes turned slightly out. Sit back and down until the thighs pass parallel, then drive through the whole foot to stand.
Form check: Knees track over the toes · Thighs past parallel · Chest stays up

Name: Squat (Deep)
How to: Squat all the way to the bottom so the hamstrings rest on the calves and hold there comfortably. Stand back up without letting the heels lift.
Form check: Full depth, heels down · Hold the bottom position · Keep the spine long

Name: Standing Calf Raise
How to: Set a loaded barbell across your upper back inside a squat rack and step out. Rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can, squeezing the calves. Rock back onto your heels and lift your toes, then rock forward onto your toes again.
Form check: Rise onto your toes, then rock back · Lift your toes at the heel end · Rock smoothly, no bouncing

Name: Standing Calf Raise (Barbell)
How to: Set a loaded barbell across your upper back and place the balls of your feet on a block or plate with heels hanging off. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing the calves hard. Lower your heels below the block for a deep stretch.
Form check: Rise to full tip-toe · Sink the heels below the block

Name: Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a sturdy object for balance and place the balls of both feet on a dumbbell handle, heels on the floor. Rise onto your toes as high as you can by squeezing the calves. Lower your heels back toward the floor under control for a full stretch.
Form check: Rise as high as you can · Steady the wobbling handle

Name: Standing Military Press (Barbell)
How to: Hold the bar at the front of the shoulders, feet hip-width, glutes and abs braced. Press the bar overhead, moving the head back slightly to clear it, then push through to a locked-out finish over the mid-foot.
Form check: Squeeze the glutes and abs, don't lean back · bar travels in a straight line over the mid-foot · full lockout with the biceps by the ears · keep the ribs down

Name: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (Cable)
How to: Grab a wide bar on a high pulley with an overhand grip wider than shoulder width and step back about two feet. Hinge your torso forward about 30 degrees with arms extended toward the pulley. Sweep the bar down to your thighs in an arc, then return under control.
Form check: Sweep the bar down in an arc · Move only at the shoulders

Name: Thruster (Kettlebell)
How to: Hold two kettlebells racked at your shoulders, feet shoulder-width. Squat down until your thighs are parallel, then drive up through the legs and press both bells overhead as you stand. Lower back to the shoulders and descend again.
Form check: Hit parallel in the squat · Drive up through the legs · Press as you stand · Lock out overhead

Name: Triceps Dip (Weighted)
Equipment: Dip bars; weight belt or vest

Name: Triceps Extension (Barbell)
How to: Lie back on an incline bench set between 45 and 75 degrees, holding a barbell with an overhand grip just inside shoulder width. Extend your arms to bring the bar overhead with elbows in. Lower the bar toward the top of your head by bending the elbows, then extend back up.
Form check: Set the bench 45 to 75 degrees · Lower the bar to the top of your head

Name: Triceps Extension (Cable)
How to: Lie on a flat bench at the end of a low pulley and hold the straight bar with a narrow overhand grip. Start with your arms extended and the bar over your face. Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, then extend to press it back up.
Form check: Keep elbows tucked and still · Lower the bar toward your forehead

Name: Triceps Extension (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand with feet shoulder width and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, arms extended. Keep your elbows in and pointing up as you lower the weight behind your head. Press back up to full lockout overhead.
Form check: Keep your elbows pointing up · Lower behind your head

Name: Triceps Extension (Machine)
How to: Adjust the seat and set your upper arms against the pads, grasping the handles. Extend your elbows to push the handles down until your arms are straight. Return under control until your elbows are bent, keeping your upper arms on the pads.
Form check: Keep upper arms on the pads · Push down to straight arms

Name: Triceps Pushdown
How to: Stand at a high pulley with the elbows pinned to the sides. Extend the arms fully down, then return under control without letting the elbows drift.
Form check: Elbows stay pinned to the sides · full extension at the bottom · don't lean over the bar to push it · control the return

Name: Triceps Rope Pushdown
How to: Attach a rope to a high pulley and grip it with palms facing each other. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides and lean the torso slightly forward. Push the rope down by extending your elbows and spread the ends apart at the bottom, then let it rise to chest height.
Form check: Pin upper arms to sides · Spread rope at the bottom

Name: Upright Row (Barbell)
How to: Grip a barbell with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder width, arms hanging so the bar rests on your thighs and your back straight. Pull the bar straight up along your body toward your collarbone, leading with your elbows. Lower it under control.
Form check: Lead with your elbows · Pull to your collarbone, no swing

Name: Upright Row (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold the dumbbells in front of the thighs. Pull them straight up along the body by leading with the elbows to about chest height, then lower under control.
Form check: Lead with the elbows, keep the weights close · don't pull above chest height · control the descent · stop if the shoulders pinch

Name: V-Sit Hold
How to: From an L-sit, compress the hips and lift the straight legs above horizontal into a V shape. Lean the shoulders slightly back to balance the weight of the legs.
Form check: Legs above horizontal · Lean the shoulders back to balance · Arms stay locked

Name: Wide Pull Up
How to: Take an overhand grip wider than shoulder width. Pull the chest toward the bar while keeping the shoulders pulled down, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Hands wider than the shoulders · Lead with the chest · Do not shorten the range

Name: Wrist Roller
How to: Stand tall gripping a loaded wrist roller with both hands, palms down. Raise your arms straight in front until they are parallel to the floor. Wind the weight up by rolling the bar hand over hand, then slowly reverse the roll to lower it back down.
Form check: Hold arms out parallel to floor · Wind hand over hand · Unwind slowly to lower
